content.title: About
content.content: Creamsicle is a creamy‑orange frozen treat on a stick, popular in the United States since the early 1970s. It features a bright orange color, a smooth creamy flavor with orange notes, and a crunchy chocolate coating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Creamsicle was introduced by Popsicle in 1971.
The name combines “cream” and the suffix “sicle” (from “popsicle”).
The original recipe used natural orange essence and real cream.
Creamsicles are often associated with summer camps and school recesses.
In some countries there are fruit‑flavored variants, but the classic remains the most popular.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The creamy portion provides a modest amount of calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Vitamin C from orange
items.content: The orange flavor contributes a small dose of vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Sugar and fat deliver fast‑acting energy, useful during active play.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Creamsicles contain a considerable amount of sugar, so they should be eaten in moderation, especially by people with diabetes.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The creamy component may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Cold treat
items.content: Because of its low temperature, the treat can cause “brain freeze” or tooth sensitivity if consumed too quickly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Creamsicles are typically eaten straight from the wrapper, allowing the frozen core to melt in the mouth. They can be stored in the freezer for up to 6 months. For a softer texture, let them sit at room temperature for a few minutes before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Creamsicles in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once removed from the packaging, avoid refreezing to maintain texture quality.
